operations.name: Walter Marks

expected.sentence:
Summoned before the court.

Charges as recorded: Contempt — for refusing, on Fifth Amendment grounds, to answer a Dade County 'subversive activities' probe.

operations.research_note: Contemporary August2,1954 National Guardian explicitly names Walter Marks, son of Charles, among people directed before Circuit Judge George E. Holt in Dade grand-jury contempt proceedings. Added judge only. Scheduled July28 appearance is not established commitment or sentence date. Florida Supreme Court 76So2d798 confirms habeas litigation involving Walter Marks but appellate counsel not assumed original prosecutors. Existing yearprecision custody preserved.

operations.name: Jesse Van Camp

expected.charges: Conspiracy to file false Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavits
expected.convicted: No — 1959 conviction reversed; acquitted at retrial September 20, 1963
expected.sentence: No imprisonment. He remained free on bail and was acquitted at retrial.

operations.research_note: Contemporary DOJ U.S. Attorneys Bulletin volume8 no2 p25 names Van Camp among November16,1956 Denver federal indictees, trial judge Alfred Arraj and Internal Security Division trial staff Broome/Worthington. Contemporary union account corroborates full judge initials. Case bail was continued; no prison interval inferred from imposed sentence, and existing retrial acquittal statement preserved. https://digicoll.lib.berkeley.edu/nanna/record/72242/files/lb001058.pdf?registerDownload=1&version=1&withMetadata=0&withWatermark=0
